notes: Focus on reducing remote attack surface (messaging, VoIP, baseband, browser).
Assume physical access by a determined attacker is out of scope.
Some mitigations require ADB or device owner privileges and may not be fully automatable.

checklist: Enable full-disk encryption
Require PIN/biometric with short lock timeout
Disable installation from unknown sources
Disable USB debugging
Keep OS and apps updated (Samsung firmware + Play system updates)
Restrict notifications on lock screen (hide sensitive content)
Enable device find/remote wipe
Harden browser: block third-party cookies, disable risky flags, prefer Firefox or Chromium with hardened config
Use privacy DNS (DoH/DoT) if available
Review app permissions and revoke unnecessary (camera, mic, SMS, call logs, location)
Enable Play Protect and periodic app scanning
Disable OEM unlock and re-lock bootloader if previously unlocked
Set strong SIM PIN and disable SIM toolkit push where possible
Disable Wi-Fi auto-connect to open or unknown networks
Disable Bluetooth visibility and turn off Bluetooth when not in use
Block sideload via package installer policies / enterprise profile where possible
Disable MMS auto-download in all messaging apps (Samsung Messages, WhatsApp, Signal, etc.)
Disable link previews and in-app browsers in messengers where possible (to reduce zero-click parsing surface)
Limit installed messaging and VoIP apps to a minimal, trusted set
Disable call recording, remote support and remote control apps not strictly required
Turn off nearby device scanning, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth scanning when not navigating
Disable developer options entirely after configuration (no USB debugging, no OEM unlock toggles)
Disable smart network switching / Wi-Fi+ that automatically joins untrusted networks
Limit background sync and backup for sensitive apps (avoid uploading full message databases)
Use a separate hardened profile or device for sensitive communications only (minimal apps, no social media)
Reboot device at least once per day to clear some in-memory spyware implants
Regularly export and clear logs for monitoring while avoiding unnecessary retention
Use strong device-level passphrase (not only pattern) and avoid showing pattern traces
Disable screen-over-other-apps and accessibility permissions for non-essential apps
Periodically review installed system apps and disable non-essential attack surface where safe (e.g., unused browsers, email clients, social apps)
Avoid clicking links in unsolicited messages; open critical URLs on a separate, non-primary device
When possible, keep Samsung Knox protections enabled and do not root the device
